h: A Local Night Out Done Right
p: Wandsworth has changed a lot in recent years. The old Young's brewery site has been transformed into the Ram Quarter, with homes, bars and restaurants, and the town centre has had a fresh lease of life. It's part of a wider stretch of south-west London that's become a popular place to live, with plenty of young professionals and families who want a good night out without heading into the centre.

Wandsworth Town station is on the line from Waterloo, with trains to Clapham Junction and beyond, and East Putney on the District line isn't far away. Buses cover the area well, and Clapham Junction, one of the busiest stations in the country, is just a short ride east. If you're driving, parking can be tricky, so public transport is usually the better option.

For groups, booking ahead is the best idea, especially at weekends. Plan your teams, decide on a few prizes, and make sure everyone knows when to arrive. It's a great way to bring together friends from across south London, and the games keep everyone involved.

With time to spare, Battersea Park is a short trip east, with its lake, gardens and the striking Peace Pagoda by the river. Battersea Power Station has been transformed into a shopping and leisure destination, with Lift 109 offering views from one of the iconic chimneys. And Putney, just to the west, has a lovely riverside where you can watch the rowers on the Thames.
